493	### 5.3 The retry loop
494	
495	`crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_activity_retry_dispatch.rs`. Five changes.
496	
497	**(a) The reason predicate.** In `nif_activity_retry.rs`, beside
498	`RETRYABLE_REASON_PREFIX` (`:32`), `is_parked_reason` (`:57`) and
499	`is_worker_lost_reason` (`:88`):
500	
501	```rust
502	const POLICY_REFUSED_REASON_PREFIX: &str = "policy_refused:";
503	pub(super) fn is_policy_refused_reason(reason: &str) -> bool { … }
504	```
505	
506	`is_retryable_reason` (`:96`) is **left alone** — a `policy_refused:` reason is
507	genuinely not `retryable:`-class, and widening that predicate would route
508	refusals through the ordinary budget, which is exactly what "hop first" forbids.
509	The doc comment at `:91-95` ("Every other prefix … is non-retryable and behaves
510	as before") is amended to name the new class as handled ahead of it.
511	
512	**(b) The refusal arm in `dispatch_with_retries`** (`:247`), placed in the loop
513	body after the worker-loss arm (`:282-287`) and **before** `failure_stand_down`
514	(`:288`) — the same position and the same shape the worker-loss class already
515	occupies. Its outcomes:
516	
517	- **Chain live** → record nonterminal refusal, record hop, bump attempt, record
518	  `ActivityStarted`, `continue` with the new queue.
519	- **Chain declared and exhausted** → record nonterminal refusal, return
520	  `RetryLoopTerminal::Failed(<policy_refused: … recorded queue sequence …>)`.
521	- **No chain declared** → record nonterminal refusal, then fall through to the
522	  ordinary retry path with `retry_eligible` true (see (c)).
523	
524	**(c) `failure_stand_down`** (`:183`) takes the policy-refusal class as
525	retry-eligible **only in the no-chain case**, and its exhaustion message must
526	begin `policy_refused:`. Artifact R1-d step 5 (lines 225-228) is explicit: *"do
527	not relabel it `exhausted:` or an engine fault."* The existing `"exhausted: spent
528	{attempt} of {max} attempts; last refusal: {reason}"` format (`:197-200`) is
529	kept for `retryable:`-class exhaustion and a `policy_refused:`-prefixed twin is
530	added for refusals. **The accounting stays inside the message; no numeric bound
531	is minted** — `policy.max_attempts` comes from `retry_policy_from_config`
532	(`nif_activity_retry.rs:280-315`) off the act's own `RetrySpec`, as the artifact
533	requires (lines 243-246).
534	
535	**(d) Refusal records are `PolicyRefused`, not `Retryable`.**
536	`RetryRecord::AttemptFailed` (`:515`) hardcodes
537	`ActivityErrorKind::Retryable` at `:580`. Artifact R1-d step 1 (lines 216-217)
538	and step 5 (line 226) both require the nonterminal refusal record to carry
539	`ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused`. So `AttemptFailed` gains an explicit kind
540	(or a sibling variant) — either way the kind is passed, never defaulted.
541	
542	**(e) Same-provider retry accounting, separated from execution identity.**
543	Artifact R1-d lines 235-241: `ActivityStarted.attempt` stays a monotonically
544	increasing identity for every actual execution *including a hop*, and the
545	authored budget must no longer be inferred from it.
546	
547	Derivation, purely from history:
548	
549	```
550	same_provider_attempt = execution_attempt − hops_recorded_for_this_ordinal
551	```
552	
553	where `hops_recorded_for_this_ordinal` counts `ActivityFallbackRouted` events
554	for the ordinal in the current run segment. `failure_stand_down` is given
555	`same_provider_attempt`; `ActivityStarted`/`ActivityFailed` keep
556	`execution_attempt`. A hop increments the execution attempt and not the budget
557	attempt, which is precisely "a queue hop is an execution but is not a
558	same-provider retry". The loop derives the base count once from the seam's
559	history at entry (the same read `activity_settled_elsewhere` (`:440`) already
560	performs) and tracks both counters in-loop thereafter, so a loop restarted after
561	a crash resumes with the right budget.
562	
563	**Delivery of the queue.** `dispatch_with_retries` currently builds each
564	delivery as `let mut delivery = request.clone(); delivery.attempt = attempt;`
565	(`:261-262`). It gains a loop-local `current_queue` initialised from
566	`request.task_queue` and reassigned on a hop, stamped as
567	`delivery.task_queue = current_queue.clone()`. `ActivityDispatch`
568	(`crates/aion/src/activity/bridge.rs:29-73`) is **not** modified.
569	
570	**Who records the FINAL terminal.** Nobody in the loop. The loop returns
571	`RetryLoopTerminal::Failed(reason)`; `spawn_completion_task` (`:51-60`) delivers
572	it; the await seam records it. `take_runtime_completion`
573	(`nif_activity_await.rs:207-226`) calls `activity_error(error.message)`
574	(`nif_activity.rs:232-238`), which builds `ActivityErrorKind::Terminal` with the
575	message verbatim. So the final event is `Terminal` with a `policy_refused:`
576	message — artifact R1-c lines 197-201 and R1-d step 4 line 221-223, already true
577	on this tree with no change. **The builder verifies this by test and does not
578	edit the await seam.**
579	
580	### 5.4 The chain reader
581	
582	New module `crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_activity_fallback.rs`, holding the
583	whole of L3's routing derivation so no existing file has to grow much:
584	
585	- `fallback_chain_from_config(config: &str) -> Vec<String>` — decodes
586	  `config.fallback`. Malformed JSON, absent, `null`, or non-array-of-string ⇒
587	  empty chain (no hop), mirroring `labels_from_config`/`resolve_task_queue`'s
588	  documented "never fail a dispatch over routing metadata" stance
589	  (`nif_activity.rs:100-107`) — with a `tracing::warn!`, never a silent drop.
590	  Carries D1's argument in its doc comment.
591	- `next_hop(chain, initial_queue, current_queue, consumed) -> Option<(usize, String)>`
592	  — the pure function: walk the authored list from position `consumed`, **skip**
593	  any entry equal to the current queue (artifact line 208-211), return the first
594	  distinct queue with **its original authored index**. Total, deterministic, no
595	  clock, no fleet state. Unit-tested exhaustively on its own.
596	- `recorded_hops(history, activity_id) -> Vec<&Event>` and
597	  `recorded_hop_queue(history, activity_id) -> Option<String>` — the latest
598	  `ActivityFallbackRouted.to_task_queue` for the ordinal, or `None`.
599	- `refused_queue_sequence(history, activity_id, initial_queue) -> Vec<String>` —
600	  the recorded initial queue followed by each hop's `to_task_queue` in recorded
601	  order. **This is what the terminal `policy_refused:` message lists**, per
602	  artifact line 302-303: *"by the recorded sequence, not by recomputing what
603	  might have happened."*
604	
605	---
606	
607	## 6. Recovery and the replay cursor
608	
609	### 6.1 The durable order (artifact R1-e lines 277-283) and its five crash boundaries
610	
611	1. record the policy-refused `ActivityFailed` for the current queue;
612	2. derive the next list position from the recorded initial queue plus prior
613	   `ActivityFallbackRouted` events and the immutable authored list;
614	3. record `ActivityFallbackRouted` before the next dispatch;
615	4. record the next `ActivityStarted`;
616	5. put the delivery on the recorded `to_task_queue`.
617	
618	Steps 1, 3 and 4 are appends through `record_retry_event`; step 2 is pure; step
619	5 is the loop's next iteration. The crash boundaries are therefore: **before 1**,
620	**between 1 and 3**, **between 3 and 4**, **between 4 and 5**, and **after 5**.
621	
622	- **Before 1** — nothing recorded; the trail dangles at the previous
623	  `ActivityStarted`. Replay exhausts the cursor and re-dispatches live on the
624	  queue `recorded_hop_queue` reports (or the initial queue if no hop yet), at
625	  the next attempt via `next_delivery_attempt`. Unchanged behaviour.
626	- **Between 1 and 3** — the refusal is recorded, no hop. Step 2 re-derives from
627	  the same inputs (recorded initial queue + recorded hops + the bound module's
628	  authored list) and reaches the same answer. Artifact line 285.
629	- **Between 3 and 4** — the hop is recorded. Recovery **reuses**
630	  `to_task_queue`; it does not derive again and does not consult live worker
631	  availability. Artifact lines 286-287. This is the boundary the whole event
632	  exists for.
633	- **Between 4 and 5** — hop and start both recorded; the attempt dangles.
634	  `dangling_attempt` (`nif_activity_retry.rs:379`) already handles this shape;
635	  the queue comes from the recorded hop.
636	- **After 5, before any terminal** — if recovery derives that no distinct hop
637	  and no configured same-provider retry remains, it must produce the same
638	  `RetryLoopTerminal::Failed` disposition with a `policy_refused:` message, and
639	  the await seam records the `Terminal`. Artifact lines 288-293: the ordinal
640	  must not dangle and no extra execution may be invented.
641	
642	### 6.2 The re-dispatch queue override — the sharpest seam in this leg
643	
644	🔴 On recovery, workflow code re-executes and
645	`dispatch_activity_with_context` (`crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_activity_dispatch.rs:301`)
646	re-resolves the queue at `:350` via `resolve_task_queue(&call.config,
647	start_time_task_queue)` — which yields the **INITIAL** queue, not the hopped-to
648	one. It then stamps that value onto both the recorded `ActivityStarted`
649	(`open_this_delivery` → `record_started`, `:281-295`) and the live
650	`ActivityDispatch` (`:385-397`). **Left as-is, a crash after a hop re-dispatches
651	on the refusing queue and history records it — the replay break the artifact's
652	R1-e exists to prevent.**
653	
654	The fix, and it is deliberately outside `resolve_task_queue` (D3): immediately
655	after `:350`, override with the recorded hop.
656	
657	```rust
658	let task_queue = super::nif_activity::resolve_task_queue(
659	    &call.config, start_time_task_queue.as_deref());
660	// R1-e: a recorded hop is a POST-FAILURE OVERRIDE of the recorded initial
661	// choice, never a fourth precedence level inside resolve_task_queue. The
662	// override reads history, so replay re-derives it identically.
663	let task_queue = super::nif_activity_fallback::recorded_hop_queue(
664	    context.history(), &activity_id).unwrap_or(task_queue);
665	```
666	
667	The same override applies on the fan-out paths, which resolve the queue at three
668	sites in `crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_collect.rs`: `fan_out_items:401`,
669	`fresh_scheduled_activity:431`, and `fan_out_items_recovered:450`. The last one
670	already reads the queue back from the recorded `ActivityScheduled` (NSTQ-3) and
671	is the established precedent for exactly this move — the hop simply takes
672	precedence over the recorded `ActivityScheduled.task_queue` there. The existing
673	history reader to mirror is
674	`nif_collect_settlement.rs::scheduled_task_queue:461`.
675	
676	`Event::ActivityScheduled` is **not** re-recorded on a hop. The artifact's order
677	lists only `ActivityFallbackRouted` then `ActivityStarted`, and
678	`ActivityStarted` carries no `task_queue` field — which is precisely why the hop
679	needs its own event. `resolve_node` (`nif_activity.rs:159`) is untouched: node
680	affinity is within-pool and a hop changes the pool, so the hop's dispatch
681	carries the same resolved node the config selects, or none.
682	
683	### 6.3 Cursor span
684	
685	`HistoryCursor::resolve_activity` (`crates/aion/src/durability/cursor.rs:297-367`)
686	walks an activity's span by matching `ActivityStarted`, a re-dispatch
687	`ActivityScheduled`, `ActivityFailed`, and the terminals, all keyed by
688	`activity_id`, and **skips** everything else in place (`_ => {}` at `:361`).
689	
690	Two changes:
691	
692	1. **Site 1's predicate** (§1.3) — the walk continues past a `PolicyRefused`
693	   failure exactly as it continues past a `Retryable` one.
694	2. **`ActivityFallbackRouted` is consumed into the span**, as a new match arm
695	   pushing to `matched` beside the `ActivityStarted` arm (`:308-313`). Artifact
696	   lines 295-297 require it: recovery and the cursor must treat the hop and the
697	   nonterminal refusal as part of the same activity span. Leaving it to the
698	   `_ => {}` skip would leave a straggler event matchable by a later command.
699	
700	`replay_inspect.rs` walks recorded history directly with no natives; its
701	`event_kind` arm (`:698` region) is all it needs beyond site 7.
702

376	/// Map a slice of `(ordinal, spec)` pairs to the durable-outbox [`FanOutItem`]s the recorder stages.
377	///
378	/// Drives the flag-ON fresh dispatch ([`NifContext::record_fan_out_dispatch`]); the stale re-arm
379	/// path ([`NifContext::rearm_outbox_pending`]) re-derives its items from recorded history instead
380	/// (see [`fan_out_items_recovered`]).
381	///
382	/// `start_time_task_queue` is the workflow's RECORDED start-time queue (#144), applied as each
383	/// member's fallback when its config selects no queue — read from history once by the caller so the
384	/// resolved queue replays deterministically.
385	fn fan_out_items(
386	    members: &[(u64, &ActivitySpec)],
387	    namespace: &str,
388	    start_time_task_queue: Option<&str>,
389	    label: &str,
390	) -> Result<Vec<FanOutItem>, String> {
391	    members
392	        .iter()
393	        .map(|(ordinal, spec)| {
394	            Ok(FanOutItem {
395	                ordinal: *ordinal,
396	                namespace: namespace.to_owned(),
397	                // NSTQ-4 (+#144): resolve each member's task queue once at this schedule seam
398	                // (member override > workflow declared default > the workflow's recorded start-time
399	                // queue > the named default) from its dispatch config, so the staged outbox row and
400	                // the recorded `ActivityScheduled` land on the chosen pool.
401	                task_queue: super::nif_activity::resolve_task_queue(
402	                    &spec.config,
403	                    start_time_task_queue,
404	                ),
405	                // NODE-4: resolve each member's OPTIONAL node affinity once at this schedule seam
406	                // (member pin, else None — no workflow default) from its dispatch config, so the
407	                // staged outbox row and the recorded `ActivityScheduled` land on the chosen node.
408	                node: super::nif_activity::resolve_node(&spec.config),
409	                activity_type: spec.name.clone(),
410	                input: payload_from_json_text(&spec.input, label)?,
411	                // NOI-0: a fresh fan-out dispatch is the first delivery of each member, attempt 1.
412	                attempt: FIRST_DELIVERY_ATTEMPT,
413	            })
414	        })
415	        .collect()
416	}
417	
418	/// Build the [`ScheduledActivity`](super::nif_activity::ScheduledActivity) for one FRESH
419	/// (non-recovered) fan-out member on the flag-OFF single-schedule path.
420	///
421	/// Resolves the task queue and OPTIONAL node once at this schedule seam (NSTQ-4 / NODE-4, same
422	/// precedence as the flag-ON fan-out and single-schedule paths), and stamps the first-delivery
423	/// attempt (NOI-0): a fresh fan-out member is its first delivery, attempt 1.
424	fn fresh_scheduled_activity(
425	    spec: &ActivitySpec,
426	    start_time_task_queue: Option<&str>,
427	    label: &str,
428	) -> Result<super::nif_activity::ScheduledActivity, String> {
429	    Ok(super::nif_activity::ScheduledActivity {
430	        activity_type: spec.name.clone(),
431	        input: payload_from_json_text(&spec.input, label)?,
432	        task_queue: super::nif_activity::resolve_task_queue(&spec.config, start_time_task_queue),
433	        node: super::nif_activity::resolve_node(&spec.config),
434	        attempt: FIRST_DELIVERY_ATTEMPT,
435	    })
436	}
437	
438	/// Map a slice of recovered `(ordinal, spec)` pairs to [`FanOutItem`]s whose `task_queue` and
439	/// OPTIONAL `node` affinity are read back from each ordinal's recorded
440	/// [`Event::ActivityScheduled`] (NSTQ-3 / NODE-3 recovery).
441	///
442	/// Unlike [`fan_out_items`] — which resolves each member's task queue and OPTIONAL node from its
443	/// live dispatch config (NSTQ-4 / NODE-4) — this re-derives the durable task queue and node from
444	/// history so the re-staged outbox row re-targets the SAME pool AND node the crashed dispatch
445	/// chose. A history recorded before the `task_queue` field existed
446	/// (or any ordinal without a recorded `ActivityScheduled`) deterministically reads back the named
447	/// default queue via the event's serde default; a history recorded before the `node` field existed
448	/// deterministically reads back `None` (no affinity), so recovery is replay-safe.
449	fn fan_out_items_recovered(
450	    members: &[(u64, &ActivitySpec)],
451	    namespace: &str,
452	    history: &[Event],
453	    label: &str,
454	) -> Result<Vec<FanOutItem>, String> {
455	    members
456	        .iter()
457	        .map(|(ordinal, spec)| {
458	            Ok(FanOutItem {
459	                ordinal: *ordinal,
460	                namespace: namespace.to_owned(),
461	                task_queue: scheduled_task_queue(history, *ordinal)
462	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| String::from(aion_core::DEFAULT_TASK_QUEUE)),
463	                // NODE-3 recovery: re-derive the OPTIONAL node affinity from history so the
464	                // re-staged outbox row re-targets the SAME node the crashed dispatch chose. A
465	                // pre-field history reads back `None` (no affinity) deterministically.
466	                node: scheduled_node(history, *ordinal),
467	                activity_type: spec.name.clone(),
468	                input: payload_from_json_text(&spec.input, label)?,
469	                // NOI-0 recovery: re-derive the attempt from the recorded `ActivityStarted` so the
470	                // re-staged dispatch keeps the SAME attempt identity. A pre-field or unrecorded
471	                // ordinal reads back the legacy sentinel / first delivery deterministically.
472	                attempt: started_attempt(history, *ordinal).unwrap_or(FIRST_DELIVERY_ATTEMPT),
473	            })
474	        })
475	        .collect()
476	}

193	        "control: an open epoch must let the loop finish normally"
194	    );
195	    let after_control = harness.history().await?.len();
196	    assert!(
197	        after_control > before,
198	        "control: an open epoch must record the attempt trail ({before} -> {after_control})"
199	    );
200	
201	    // Now close the epoch, exactly as `Engine::shutdown` and `Drop` both do.
202	    harness.seam.engine_tasks.begin_close();
203	    assert!(
204	        !harness.seam.engine_tasks.is_epoch_open(),
205	        "the epoch must actually be closed, or what follows measures nothing"
206	    );
207	
208	    let dispatcher = ScriptedRetryDispatcher::new(vec![
209	        Err("retryable:stream reset".to_owned()),
210	        Ok(r#""done""#.to_owned()),
211	    ]);
212	    let outcome = super::dispatch_with_retries(
213	        &(Arc::clone(&dispatcher) as Arc<dyn ActivityDispatcher>),
214	        &harness.seam,
215	        &harness.request,
216	    )
217	    .await;
218	
219	    assert!(
220	        matches!(outcome.terminal, super::RetryLoopTerminal::SettledElsewhere),
221	        "a closed epoch must stand the loop down rather than deliver an outcome for a run this \
222	         process is no longer the writer for"
223	    );
224	    assert_eq!(
225	        harness.history().await?.len(),
226	        after_control,
227	        "NOTHING may be appended after the epoch closes: an append here is the #119 \
228	         second-writer breach — the survivor either takes a SequenceConflict or replays a \
229	         command against an event the live run never issued"
230	    );
231	    Ok(())
232	}

result_summary.response:
Committed scoped core/event/projection work as `d02232de` (`feat: record policy fallback routing events`).

Implemented:
- `ActivityError::is_settled()` with explicit non-complement documentation and a `PolicyRefused` unit test.
- Settlement predicate conversions at cursor, collect terminal scan, collect race winner, fan-out ordinal resolution, live executor guard, and replay-inspect guard; guard errors now name the offending kind.
- `Event::ActivityFallbackRouted` with the exact durable fields and no serde defaults; `Event::envelope()` updated.
- Recorder-only `record_activity_fallback_routed` method.
- Cursor consumes fallback hops into the activity span; cursor/replay/resolver event-kind projections updated.
- Status/current-step, delegated family, continue-as-new, server selector, ops timeline and known-variant projections updated.
- TypeScript bindings regenerated canonically with `AION_UPDATE_BINDINGS=1 cargo test -p aion-core export_ops_console_wire_types` (not hand-edited).
- Ops exhaustive event fixture added; fallback route stays on the activity lane and does not become cancellation/terminal state.

Verification observed:
- `cargo test -p aion-core`: 118 unit tests + 1 doctest passed, 0 failed/ignored.
- `cargo check -p aion-rs -p aion-server --all-targets`: passed.
- `bun test ...timeline.test.ts ...timelineVariants.test.ts`: 24 passed, 0 failed.
- `bun run typecheck`: could not execute because `tsc` is absent (`/usr/bin/bash: tsc: command not found`); this is an environment/tooling blocker, not a type diagnostic.
- `git diff --cached --check`: clean before commit.

Shared-worktree overlap disclosed:
- Required settlement site 5 (`nif_activity_retry.rs::activity_settled`) is changed in the shared worktree to `error.is_settled()`, but that file also contains the parent runtime implementation. I intentionally excluded it from `d02232de` to avoid committing the parent's unrelated in-progress routing changes. Parent was notified to preserve that hunk in its runtime commit.

Remaining binding-test gaps for parent integration:
- I did not add seven separate per-site focused tests nor the explicit `resolution_from_matched` coupling test. The semantic core has a direct `PolicyRefused` three-valued test, and compilation/existing suites pass, but the brief's one-test-per-site teeth still need adding before final delivery.

Over-500-line disclosures:
- `recorder.rs` gained only the required recorder method/doc.
- `cursor.rs` gained only compiler/behavior-required hop-span and predicate/event-kind changes.
- `nif_collect_settlement.rs` gained only the two predicate conversions and site-decision comments.
- Existing oversized ops `timeline.test.ts` gained the compiler/exhaustive-fixture-required new event fixture and family row.
- `nif_activity_retry.rs` overlap was not included in this commit.

1	//! Shared gate and runner for the tests in this crate that shell out to the
2	//! real `gleam` CLI.
3	//!
4	//! Task #74. This file is a **port** of the cure landed for `aion-awl` at
5	//! commit `8fb4c153` (`crates/aion-awl/tests/test_support/gleam.rs`). The
6	//! version it replaces announced its skip with `println!` and accepted a zero
7	//! exit from `gleam build` as proof, so three different outcomes were fused
8	//! into one indistinguishable `ok` line. They are now kept apart:
9	//!
10	//! - `gleam` is **absent** — the test skips, and announces the skip loudly
11	//!   enough that it can never be read as a pass (see [`announce`]).
12	//! - `gleam` **rejects the Gleam under test** — the test FAILS, named as a code
13	//!   defect. That is the signal these proofs exist for.
14	//! - `gleam` fails inside its own **dependency layer** (the Hex registry) —
15	//!   the build is retried a bounded number of times, and if every attempt
16	//!   fails the test still FAILS, named as an infrastructure failure. It is
17	//!   never skipped: a fetch failure that skipped would let the proof pass
18	//!   while proving nothing, which is the exact vacuity this cycle is about.
19	//!
20	//! Classification decides **whether to retry** and **what the message calls
21	//! the failure**. It can never turn a failure into a pass: both branches end
22	//! in `Err`. That is why an unrecognised failure is classified as a code
23	//! defect — the safe polarity is "blame the code, make a human look".
24	//!
25	//! # Why this file is copied rather than shared
26	//!
27	//! `#[path = "test_support/gleam.rs"] mod ...` resolves relative to the
28	//! including test file, so a single shared copy would mean each crate reaching
29	//! across a crate boundary with `../../<other-crate>/tests/...`. That is a
30	//! path hack, and it would break `cargo package` for these published crates:
31	//! `tests/` is packaged, and a source file outside the crate root is not.
32	//! The copies are therefore kept byte-identical and pinned that way by
33	//! [`the_shared_gleam_support_copies_have_not_diverged`], which fails in every
34	//! crate the moment one copy is edited alone.
35	//!
36	//! That pin checks the copies it was told about, so on its own it cannot see a
37	//! copy nobody wrote down — the list it verifies is the same list it derives
38	//! its expectation from. [`every_gleam_support_file_is_classified`] supplies
39	//! the other half by enumerating the filesystem and requiring every `gleam.rs`
40	//! it finds to be accounted for, so the three lists together are a statement
41	//! about **every** copy that exists rather than only the intended ones.
